questions.enonce_markdown: Name the cellular components of blood and give a function for each. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Red blood cells (erythrocytes):** they carry **oxygen** from the lungs to the tissues, as oxyhaemoglobin (and carry some carbon dioxide back).
2. **White blood cells (leucocytes):** they **defend** the body against disease: phagocytes engulf and digest bacteria (phagocytosis), and lymphocytes make **antibodies** and antitoxins.
3. **Platelets (thrombocytes):** they help the **clotting** of blood at a wound, which stops bleeding and prevents the entry of germs.

questions.enonce_markdown: Draw a large and neatly labelled diagram to show the longitudinal section of the human heart. *(8 marks)*
In tabular form, distinguish between blood plasma and lymph. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Blood plasma | Lymph |
|---|---|
| Liquid part of the blood, found in the blood vessels (arteries, veins, capillaries) | Fluid found in the lymph vessels and lymph nodes |
| Contains no cells (the blood cells are suspended in it) | Contains lymphocytes; no red blood cells and no platelets |
| Contains a large amount of plasma proteins | Contains a smaller amount of proteins |
| Contains more oxygen and digested food | Contains less oxygen and less digested food, but more carbon dioxide and wastes |
| Pale yellow (straw-coloured) | Colourless |
| Moves under high pressure, pumped by the heart | Moves slowly under low pressure, by the squeezing of skeletal muscles and the valves of the lymph vessels |
| Transports hormones, digested food, urea and carbon dioxide | Returns tissue fluid to the blood and carries fats absorbed in the lacteals |
